newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ARA barges still tied-up despite smoother delivery.
newsitem.headline: ARA barges still tied-up despite smoother delivery.

text.p: Barges in the ARA market are still largely tied up with the record IPE delivery, but shipowners report the loadings are proceeding more smoothly than last week.
"There are not so many problems now, although most barges are busy until the end of the month," one barge supplier said.

The congestion comes during the record 865,100 tonne delivery of gas oil against expired November IPE futures and the duel between two trading houses who are contracted to exchange the bulk of the volume.
Trouble was most extreme at the start of the 15-day delivery period with queues and logistical difficulties putting back the schedule by two to three days, barge suppliers said.

Logistical problems have been smoothed, they say, but the backlog and the sheer size of the operation remain and traders seeking barges face large headaches unless they are prepared to accept a December loading date. Prices, already about 40 percent higher than 10 days ago, are set to rise further.

"A lot of barges are occupied. Even though things have improved, it's physically almost impossible to load everything and we've had people from all over asking us if we have any spare (vessels)," one barge supplier said.
Difficulties are still most extreme in Amsterdam where much of the deliveries are and were due to take place.
"Antwerp is doing quite well, but Amsterdam is still quite messy and the rest of the market is suffering for sure," one barge supplier said.

On Friday, AIC, the main short in the November IPE gas oil contract, said that Cargill, the main long, was behind its nominations for the second five-day delivery window which ends at midnight on Monday.
An AIC spokesman said Cargill was 38 percent short on its nominations in the Amsterdam area and 60 percent short in the Antwerp area.
He said Cargill had indicated it intended to lift 260,000 tonnes in the second November 21-25 period.
Earlier in the week, AIC said Cargill had failed to lift the required volume of gas oil in the first five day period of November 16-20.
Cargill said on Thursday there had been some problems in the first five-day delivery period but it hoped to resolve these through IPE channels.
